item.description: After Jensen Huang’s resignation, it can’t possibly be $960,000.

item.description: Also the Anthropic IPO book, LLM index fund recommendations and the Head of Macro guy.
item.dc:creator: Matthew S Levine

item.title: Jensen Huang Resigns: He Failed Nvidia Long Before His Affair
item.description: “He’s irreplaceable,” Larry Ellison said.
item.dc:creator: Beth Kowitt

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s Downfall Knocks American AI Onto a Different Course
item.description: As the unthinkable became the inevitable, and Jensen Huang’s position as chief executive officer of Nvidia Corp. lurched from precarious to untenable, attention now turns to what American artificial intelligence looks like without its leather-jacketed champion. One man’s infidelities risk sending the country on a different course.
item.dc:creator: Dave Lee

item.title: Colom’s Mississippi Win Shows a Seismic Shift in the Deep South
item.description: “Mississippi Matters.”
item.dc:creator: Nia-Malika Henderson

item.title: China Is the Biggest Loser From Jensen Huang’s Downfall
item.description: Jensen Huang’s resignation from Nvidia Corp. may give the company he’s led for three decades a path out of the mess he created. For China’s artificial-intelligence industry, the fallout is just beginning.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Thorbecke

item.title: Anthropic IPO: Amodei Can’t Out-Stubborn the Market
item.description: Anthropic PBC has benefited from the single-minded focus of a leader who doesn’t waver from his decisions. But that advantage could become a liability as it speeds toward an initial public offering in the middle of a febrile market, with the Nasdaq having fallen about 6% in the past month and the possible ouster of Nvidia Corp.’s Jensen Huang sapping confidence in the artificial intelligence trade.
item.dc:creator: Parmy Olson

item.title: California’s Prop 40 Defeat Doesn’t End the Wealth Tax Debate
item.description: Silicon Valley’s billionaires spent a record sum on this year’s midterms — and, for the most part, it was a poor investment. Voters slapped restrictions on data centers, and many Democratic candidates trounced their Republican opponents by using tech companies as a foil, promising to rein in the “oligarchs” who run them.
item.dc:creator: Erika D. Smith

item.title: The COP31 Talks Show the Disaster of a Post-American World
item.description: If you want to glimpse the fate of our world after the abdication of American leadership, as humanity struggles to cope with its biggest problems, cast your eye toward Antalya, Turkey. This is where delegations from some 200 countries have gathered for COP31, the 31st conference of the United Nations treaty to slow down climate change.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Kluth

item.title: Mexican Tourism to the US Defies Trump-Era Decline
item.description: Since Donald Trump started his second term as president in January 2025, international visits to the US have fallen more than 6%. There was a modest uptick during the men’s soccer World Cup in June and July, but full numbers for August and partial ones for September from the US International Trade Administration show a resumption of the decline.
item.dc:creator: Justin Fox

item.title: Defense Spending Can’t Be Hostage to the Iran Standoff
item.description: The political drama resulting from Democrats’ landslide midterm victory will start in early December with budget talks, especially those focused on defense spending. The plot is as tangled as a daytime soap opera. Legislators have already taken a stab at removing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and the Iran war hangs over negotiations like a dark, ominous cloud.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Black

item.title: The Colorado River’s Problems Run Too Deep for El Niño to Solve
item.description: The Colorado River watershed is sort of the inverse of an iceberg’s tip: While a small volume of ice above the surface suggests a massive volume below, the Colorado’s absence of water above the ground hints at an even vaster void underneath.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gongloff

item.title: Immigration Policy Could Cost US Its AI Lead Over China
item.description: The White House says everything must be done to maintain America’s lead over China in artificial intelligence, whether by blocking access to advanced semiconductors or refusing to pause research at frontier labs. Yet one of the biggest threats to that progress may be the administration’s own immigration proposals.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: Russell Brand and David Walliams Had Lots of People Around Them Too
item.description: Three cameos stand out in the recent spate of celebrity sex misconduct cases. In one a teenager is embraced by an older TV star at a celebrity quiz night, beside a table of famous faces. She looks uncomfortable and out of place. In another, a woman in her 20s goes to a party in a busy bar in London’s Soho, where a famous comedian gropes her breasts within a minute of meeting her. In the last, a 17-year-old girl is aboard a yacht in St. Tropez with the close associate of a superrich financier cel
item.dc:creator: Rosa Prince

item.title: Skydance Can't Afford DC Studio's Cinematic Universe
item.description: The hierarchy of power in the DC Universe is about to change … again. DC Studios co-CEOs James Gunn and Peter Safran will step down on Dec. 1 and be replaced by former Marvel Studios executive Jeremy Latcham. It’s a surprising move, especially when you consider that Gunn and Safran were recently named to Skydance’s executive leadership team post-merger.
item.dc:creator: Miles Surrey

item.title: Democrats 2026 Wins Come as Sunbelt's Political Power Grows
item.description: Like the cavalry in an old Western, a new generation of Democrats has arrived just in time to restore the party’s competitiveness in the Sunbelt. Democrats last week recorded their best 21st-century showing across an arc of Sunbelt states, including North and South Carolina, Georgia, Texas, Arizona and Nevada. Democrats also picked up a Senate seat in Mississippi and mounted unexpectedly strong bids for another Senate seat in Louisiana as well as the Alabama governorship.
item.dc:creator: Ronald Brownstein

item.title: Forget Nvidia. Anthropic Is the AI Trade’s Litmus Test
item.description: For an industry that needs to spend at least $30 billion just to build a data center that handles one gigawatt of computing power, access to financing is key.
item.dc:creator: Shuli Ren

item.title: History Is Calling Europe on Ukraine. Can it Answer?
item.description: There are reasons to believe an opportunity now exists to reach a peace deal on Ukraine. There’s the mere fact that Russia agreed to attend a new round of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi this week, the approach of a new, less Moscow-friendly US Congress, the soaring casualty rates among Vladimir Putin’s troops and the unbearable toll on Ukraine’s cities and economy. The rational takeaway from all this, that we are on the threshold of a pact to end the war, is unfortunately misleading.
item.dc:creator: Marc Champion

item.title: AI, Anthropic: Claude And Muse Won’t Revolutionize Your Finances
item.description: US credit cards provide a perfect frontline for the nascent battle between banks and artificial intelligence companies: If people are ever going to let software agents loose on their finances, reward programs are an obvious place to start. I suspect, however, that old habits of caution and inertia will prove hard to overcome.
item.dc:creator: Paul J. Davies

item.title: Nvidia: Ritual CEO Sacrifice Is Looming Over Jensen Huang
item.description: Markets may be overstating the wider risk to AI.
item.dc:creator: John Authers
